questions.q: How do seismic waves help us understand the interior of the Earth?
answer: Since we cannot see inside the Earth, seismic waves produced by earthquakes are the most important indirect source of information about its interior.

answer.text: There are two main body waves. Primary or P-waves are the fastest and can pass through solids, liquids and gases. Secondary or S-waves are slower and can travel only through solids, not through liquids.

As these waves pass through the Earth, their speed and direction change at boundaries where the density of material changes. These sudden changes, called discontinuities, mark the divisions between the crust, mantle and core.

Above all, S-waves fail to appear in a certain zone on the far side of the Earth, called the shadow zone. Because S-waves cannot pass through liquid, this proves that the outer core is in a liquid state.

answer: Thus seismic waves reveal the layered structure of the Earth's interior.
